sources.title: France–Monaco Neighbourhood Convention of 18 May 1963
sources.officialityEvidence: Legimonaco publishes the consolidated Convention as in force on 19 July 2026. Article 2 makes Monaco's under-three-month foreigner regime identical to France's.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Dans la Principauté, le régime d'entrée et de circulation des étrangers est identique à celui qui s'applique à ces étrangers en France.

sources.title: Sovereign Ordinance No. 3.153: conditions of entry and stay of foreigners
sources.officialityEvidence: Legimonaco publishes Monaco's current foreign-entry Ordinance. Article 1 requires the French-access travel documents, visas and authorisations for a foreigner entering Monaco.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Tout étranger ... doit être muni d'un passeport valable ... permettant l'accès ... en France.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2018/1806, consolidated 30 December 2025
sources.officialityEvidence: EUR-Lex shows the current consolidated Regulation in force from 30 December 2025. Articles 3–4 and Annexes I–II establish France's short-stay visa split.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Nationals of third countries listed in Annex I shall be required to be in possession of a visa.

sources.title: Directive 2004/38/EC: right of entry for Union citizens
sources.officialityEvidence: EUR-Lex publishes Directive 2004/38. Article 5 establishes that Union citizens entering a Member State are not subject to an entry visa or equivalent formality.
sources.supportingExcerpt: No entry visa or equivalent formality may be imposed on Union citizens.

sources.title: Schengen Borders Code: persons with equivalent free-movement rights
sources.officialityEvidence: EUR-Lex hosts the consolidated Schengen Borders Code. Its free-movement definition includes third-country nationals with equivalent rights under Union and Member-State agreements.
sources.supportingExcerpt: third-country nationals ... enjoy rights of free movement equivalent to those of Union citizens

sources.title: EU visa agreements with non-EU countries
sources.officialityEvidence: The Council's official register, last reviewed 3 March 2026, states that Nauru's Annex-II exemption does not apply until a waiver agreement is concluded.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Visa-free regime will apply only once Nauru and EU have concluded a visa waiver agreement.

sources.title: European Travel Information and Authorisation System: current status
sources.publisher: European Commission, Directorate-General for Migration and Home Affairs
sources.officialityEvidence: The Commission's Smart Borders page reports the current operational status of ETIAS, the planned authorisation for visa-exempt third-country travellers.
sources.supportingExcerpt: ETIAS is currently not in operation and no applications for travel authorisations are collected at this point.

policies.title: EU ordinary passports: visa-free short visit to Monaco
policies.summary: For a short visit, Monaco applies the same foreigner entry and circulation regime as France. Union citizens need no French entry visa, therefore have a visa-free visitor route to Monaco.
conditions: This is an ordinary visit of under three months under Monaco's France-aligned entry regime; Monaco is not a Schengen Member State.
Use a valid passport or national identity card as applicable. Admission, document validity, purpose, funds, public-order and route checks remain applicable.
No separate Monegasque eVisa, ETA or visa-on-arrival route is established by the reviewed official sources.

policies.title: Visa-exempt French-access ordinary passports: visa-free short visit to Monaco
policies.summary: For a short visit, Monaco applies the same foreigner entry and circulation regime as France. These ordinary passports are visa-exempt for the French access leg under Annex II or equivalent free-movement arrangements and therefore have a visa-free visitor route to Monaco.
conditions: This is a Monaco visit of under three months; the French/Schengen access leg is limited to no more than 90 days in any 180-day period.
Biometric passports are required for AL, BA, GE, MD, ME, MK, RS, UA and XK. Taiwan requires an identity-card number in the passport; HK and MO require their named SAR passports.

CH, IS, LI and NO follow equivalent free-movement treatment for the French access leg. Residence permits, refugee/stateless documents, border permits, school groups, paid activity, crew and special passports are not normalized into this ordinary-passport baseline.
No current source establishes a separate nationality-wide Monaco visitor visa rule for minors. A Monaco circulation document for a minor resident is a residence document, not a visitor-access rule.
ETIAS is not operating on the research date. No separate Monegasque eVisa, ETA or visa-on-arrival route is established by the reviewed official sources.

policies.title: Nauru ordinary passport: advance visa required pending EU waiver agreement
policies.summary: Nauru remains subject to the French short-stay visa requirement because its Annex-II exemption is conditional on an EU–Nauru waiver agreement that is not concluded.
conditions: This is a French/Schengen advance-visa requirement applied in Monaco under the France–Monaco short-stay convention, not a separately issued Monegasque visitor visa.
Nauru's Annex-II listing does not currently create a waiver: the Regulation's footnote makes it conditional, and the Council says the agreement remains unconcluded.
No Monegasque eVisa, ETA or visa-on-arrival route is established by the reviewed official sources. Final French and Monaco admission decisions remain separate.

policies.title: Annex I ordinary passports: advance visa required for Monaco short visit
policies.summary: For a short visit, Monaco applies the French foreigner-entry regime. These passports require the applicable French/Schengen advance visa; a visa valid for France is valid in Monaco.
conditions: This is the French/Schengen advance-visa requirement carried into Monaco's short-stay foreigner regime, not a separately issued Monegasque visitor visa. Visas valid for France are valid in Monaco.
The Monaco visit is under three months. The French/Schengen access leg follows its short-stay rules; residence permits, long-stay visas and special documents are not flattened into this baseline.

The source law provides distinct rules for stays over three months and Monegasque residence permits; those are not visitor-visa waivers. ETIAS is not operating and no Monegasque eVisa, ETA or visa-on-arrival route is established by the reviewed official sources.
